# SOP-P2-L1-01 Line startup - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Purpose
This procedure describes the controlled startup sequence for the Hot Forge line at P2-L1, covering permit preconditions, personnel protective equipment, stepwise actions, operational rationale, examples of expected observations, and records required for compliance. It applies to operators and maintenance staff responsible for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03. See related documents SB-1001, SB-1030, and SOP-P2-L1-04 for maintenance details, blast cabinet servicing, and shutdown procedures.

Preconditions
1. All tags, lockout devices, and isolation points have been verified cleared per SB-1001.  
2. Plant control room has acknowledged line status as ready.  
3. Required spare parts and consumables are present as identified in SOP-P2-L1-04 for initial run.  
4. Environmental monitoring is in normal state and there are no pending area alarms referencing EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

PPE
1. Leather or heat-rated gloves, face shield, flame-retardant jacket, and hearing protection appropriate to Hot Forge operations.  
2. Respiratory protection as required by SB-1030 when servicing or verifying shot blast systems.  
3. Steel toe boots and eye protection for all personnel on the shop floor.

Startup Steps (numbered sequence)
1. Pre-start inspection
   - Walk the line and visually inspect EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03 for loose panels, debris, or obvious damage.  
   - Confirm that access panels are secured and guards are in place. Rationale: early visual detection prevents unplanned stops and safety incidents.

2. Verify critical fasteners
   - Confirm maintenance log shows mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) set to 430 N·m. If log absent, verify torque at specified torque value prior to energizing EQ-P2-L1-RR01. Rationale: correct clamp torque ensures mandrel stability and prevents ring distortion during rolling.

3. Blast cabinet system check
   - Verify shot blast cabinet operation readiness for EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Confirm that the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa and that the alarm state is normal. If alarm persists, follow SB-1030 to clear and verify collector performance. Rationale: dust collector performance directly affects air quality and media containment during blast operations.

4. Heater and induction oven verification
   - Confirm IH control interlocks are functional per SOP-P2-L1-04 before enabling EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Rationale: induction heating interlocks protect against overcurrent and control faults.

5. Control system sequence enable
   - From the control room, enable line PLC sequence for Hot Forge. Observe soft interlocks and listen for abnormal noises. Rationale: staged enable reduces risk of mechanical engagement under load.

6. Dry run with no charge
   - Run the line through mechanical motions without load to validate kinematic movement and controls. Observe bearings, belts, and roll surfaces for smooth operation. Example observation: no abnormal vibration at roll shafts and consistent return stroke on radial roll. Rationale: detecting mechanical anomalies before loading limits scrap and damage.

7. Low-load trial
   - Introduce a single test piece per operator instruction and verify clamp engagement, heating profile communication, and blast cabinet capture performance. Monitor for any alarms. Rationale: real-load validation confirms integrated system behavior.

8. Full-rate enable
   - Upon successful low-load trial, enable nominal production feed per line routing. Maintain observation for the first production cycle for consistent dimensions and surface quality. Rationale: early batch validation prevents escalation of quality issues.

9. Alarm response readiness
   - Assign an operator responsibility to monitor EH&S and machine alarms. If the dust collector pressure drop alarm for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 triggers at 1240 Pa, stop feed to the blast cabinet and shift to manual containment per SB-1030. Rationale: prompt response maintains air quality and prevents equipment overloading.

10. Communication and handover
   - Notify control room and floor supervision when the line reaches stable production. Confirm any outstanding issues logged for maintenance.

Step Rationale and Examples
- Mandrel clamp torque rationale: specified clamp torque prevents slippage and concentricity errors. Example: a correctly torqued mandrel yields repeatable ring thickness and eliminates rework associated with eccentric rings.
- Dust collector alarm rationale: maintaining the specified alarm point allows predictable maintenance scheduling and prevents particulate crossover into downstream processes. Example: a triggered dust collector alarm at the specified value requires filter inspection or media rebalancing as recorded in SB-1030.

Records to Keep
1. Startup checklist with operator name, date, and signature. Include verification entries for mandrel clamp bolt torque and dust collector pressure drop alarm with the exact values recorded.  
2. Torque verification certificate for the mandrel clamp bolt on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 indicating 430 N·m.  
3. Blast cabinet service and alarm log for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 showing the dust collector pressure drop alarm threshold and any alarm events at 1240 Pa.  
4. Control room log entry indicating time of enable, low-load trial outcome, and handover confirmation.  
5. Any nonconformance reports or quality hold tags issued during startup, cross-referenced to SB-1001.

Sign-off
Operator name: ______________________  
Operator signature: ___________________  
Supervisor name: _____________________  
Supervisor signature: __________________  
Date: _______________________________

References
- SB-1001  
- SB-1030  
- SOP-P2-L1-04

Change History
Revision: Rev E — current document revision.
